title: The Canal Lock Rescue
story:
The morning sun rose over the river valley, casting long shadows across the concrete irrigation canals winding past the orange groves. James and Nico followed the narrow rim of the water channel as it cut south through the agricultural fields. The air was cool and crisp, carrying the sharp scent of damp moss and fallen citrus. Nico was practically dancing ahead, his large ears twitching at every splash of water. Near a low concrete canal lock where water rushed noisily through a rusted metal sluice gate, Nico halted, fixated on a bright flash of metal trapped against the churned spray—a crumpled foil wrapper bobbing along the wet ledge.

Before James could reach out, Nico leaped toward the glittering lure. His tiny paws skidded across algae-slick masonry, and with a sharp squeak of terror, the deer mouse slipped over the drop into the fast-flowing spillway. Panic seized James. James had seen rushing mountain streams in the foothills. James had seen quiet canal towpaths in Oakhaven. But James had never seen his small companion vanish so quickly into churning foam. He dropped into his grounding ritual, closing his eyes for a split second to count three distinct sounds: the deafening roar of the sluice, the wet slap of water against iron, and Nico’s muffled squeak. Opening his eyes, James unclipped the spool of wooden kite twine—the strong thread from the kite festival in Aldea San Gabriel—and cast the line down into the tumbling white foam.

"Hold on!" James squeaked into the roar, bracing his feet against the concrete edge. Nico thrashed wildly, his wet claws snagging the twisted threads just as the current dragged him toward the dark mouth of the lower drain. With careful, steady pulls, James reeled the line back, hauling the shivering mouse up the sheer masonry wall to dry ground. Nico lay panting on the moss, soaked and quivering, while James checked his satchel; the leather pouch housing his green sea-glass had scuffed roughly against the sharp stone, though the polished glass inside remained whole.

James safely pulled Nico from the canal spillway using his kite twine, and by dusk the duo reached a dry evening campsite to reconcile their shaken spirits. Nestled beneath the wooden rafters of an old stone cart shed at the edge of a quiet cornfield, they rested in the gathering twilight. Nico curled tightly against James’s side, wrapped in a warm fold of indigo wool to stave off the night chill. Looking out over the tranquil river valley as the first stars appeared, James felt a deep, quiet relief, knowing their bond had survived the trial of the rushing water.
location: Stone cart shed at the edge of a cornfield beyond the orange groves
